title: Six-class secp256k1 rho with 256-walk product groups at 125.834449

claims.statement: A conditional analytical bound for the full-production secp256k1 ECDLP under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000): the six-class parallel rho procedure in proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run within 2^125.834449 target-group-operation equivalents and, under disclosed heuristics H1, C and P1, recovers the exponent with probability at least 0.39000001. It builds on b14e7c12 and its listed dependencies. The forward product and reverse update loops use 256-walk groups, while pass1 and fused loop A remain 128-walk groups. Their main-path prices are 169.50390625 and 337.50390625 instructions per walk, and the ordinary-step price is 34849/64 + 1155/256 + 26333/2^23 instructions. The fixed round charge conservatively includes 127 loop A and 255 each of product and reverse-update tail walks. The work bound is unconditional on C and P1; success remains heuristic. The shipped experiment and certificate describe their checks and limitations in evidence.md. This is an analytical bound, not a practical recovery implementation.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule. Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the walk of proof.md 5.1 on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with node routing, and a check that the (1, 256) and production compare rules reach the same endpoints. Kernels (evidence.md items 1-9): limb ports against big integers; the shipped loops, both copies of loop A and the arrival rows run by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, big-integer dx and the exact canonical rule, every stub entered and every returned borrow count checked; counts and the ledger recomputed; both census rules recomputed from census-corr.json and census-p1.json, each with a run prefix re-walked. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^23 concurrent walks.
